# Monospace from Directus: The governed API layer for every app, person, and agent

Monospace from Directus is a governed API layer that sits between enterprise data and everyone who builds on it: connect any data source once, and developers, business teams, and AI agents all get live, read-write access under the same granular permissions model, with no data copied or moved. Because it introspects schemas and queries in real time, even legacy databases get modern interfaces generated directly from them, exactly as they are — no rebuild required.

## What exactly does Monospace put between your data and your builders? [...] In short, Monospace bets enterprise data should be queried where it lives — governed per caller, per row, and per field — not copied into another store first. If your roadmap has agents acting on live systems or legacy databases that cannot be rebuilt, weigh it alongside the Product Hunt launch discussion flagged in Directus's GA launch announcement. Start with the free tier and the Docker quick start on Monospace, connect one real source, and see how far a single governed API takes you.

## Sources [...] Through four doors into the same layer: a REST API, a typed SDK, an MCP server, and a visual Data Studio. Developers query and mutate data through the REST engine with recursive relational includes, or use the typed SDK with CLI codegen so calls are type-checked against the instance's real schema — a workflow documented in the official agent-skills bundle, alongside auth, workspace bootstrapping, and schema discovery. Agents get governed access through one MCP server across all systems, with per-agent identities, limits, and logs, while business users query live data in natural language and every action lands in a shared audit log. A Chinese-language launch review singles out agents reading and writing live databases with effectively no delay as the standout capability.

Scoping access for agents is another issue that many enterprises have kicked the can on, knowing they’ll have to solve it someday.

A unified API layer doesn’t make that problem go away. It gives you one place to solve it — once, instead of once per system, per application, per agent. Monospace is one such solution.

Check out the docs and get started building your unified API layer today.
